Collaborate with project teams to develop visual storytelling concepts that communicate technical and operational goals. jobs.description: Employer: Virginia Department of Transportation Expires: 10/03/2026 Are you looking for a Roadmap for your future? VDOT’s Internship Program focuses on introducing undergraduate and graduate students to the importance of public service while understanding the critical needs of our organization through paid summer work experience. Candidates must be at least a rising sophomore (or equivalent) to be eligible to apply. The program provides for guided real work experience in various occupational disciplines related to engineering, and other functional areas within VDOT. Learning focuses on technical and self-leadership skills needed for the individual and potentially for VDOT. Depending on VDOT’s business needs and performance, interns may have the opportunity to extend their internship into the academic year.The selected intern will report directly to the Assistant Resident Engineer - Land Use at the Warrenton Residency and will be granted the opportunity to gain hands-on experience observing developmental plan reviews, rezoning applications, subdivision plats and permit applications.__Job DescriptionPerform special duties as assigned. As a student, engage and participate in planned and education-related work experiences that integrate the knowledge and theory gained in the academic setting with practical application and skill development in the workplace. How you will contribute:Communication: Communicate with VDOT staff as well as external contacts and consultants. Proactively resolve issues at the lowest level. Project a positive VDOT image. Keep supervisor advised of important development and field observations.Engineering Technology: Apply principles and practices of engineering technology to assigned programs areas. Interpret policies and procedures and apply in daily work assignments.Equipment Maintenance: Perform routine maintenance and repairs on testing equipment. Follow appropriate guidelines for equipment storage, use, and transport.Perform Duties as Assigned:Project Documentation: Prepare and maintain daily documentation of project activities. Ensure documentation is submitted and is completed. Avoid project delays and solve project related matters.Record Keeping : Maintains accurate records for all project activities. Enters and updates data to meet required deadlines and requirements. Interprets and applies relevant policies and procedures.What will make you successful:Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing. Ability to perform manual labor (securing, handling, and preparing materials samples). Ability to read and interpret engineering plans and specifications. Knowledge of mathematics up to and including algebra and geometry.Skill in the use of computers, software applications to include MS Office, and smart phones. Minimum Qualifications:Currently enrolled full-time in an Associate’s degree program or higher.Have a basic knowledge of engineering principles.Must be at least 18 years of age by the start of employment.Must maintain a full-time graduate status taking 9 or more credit hours per semester at a college/university before and following internship.Must maintain a full-time undergraduate status taking 12 or more credit hours per semester at a community college or 4-year college/university before and following internship.Additional Considerations:A combination of training, experience, or education in Engineering, or related field desired.Ability to anticipate problems, provide solutions, follow instructions, learn quickly, and collaborate with teammates.Ability to make quality and timely decisions.Ability to work independently and in teams.

jobs.title: Instrumentation & Controls Intern at Arcadis
jobs.description: Employer: Arcadis Expires: 10/03/2026 Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.Role description:Arcadis is looking for an Instrumentation & Controls (I&C) Intern with an interest in the municipal water/wastewater industry to join our growing Resilience team in Columbus, OH for Summer 2027. As an Instrumentation and Controls Intern, you will collaborate with our experienced team of professionals, providing technical and design consulting services with a focus on instrumentation, controls systems, and associated network and communications infrastructure for municipal water and wastewater conveyance and treatment facilities. As an I&C Intern, you will work in a collaborative environment, focusing on evaluating and designing control system solutions that align with client needs.Role accountabilities:Prepare technical memorandums and develop comprehensive design criteriaCraft SCADA system architectures, communication system and network designs, process and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), SCADA network diagrams, and process control functional narratives.Create specifications, control schematics, panel layout diagrams, interconnection diagrams, and other I&C design documentsCoordinate with process, mechanical, and electrical engineers assigned to the projectPerform engineering services during the construction phase, which involves reviewing equipment and software submittals, analyzing shop drawings, and responding to contractor RFIs (requests for information).As an intern, you may also have the opportunity to join our team while conducting field inspections and identify deviations from design, perform general quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) of completed work, and monitor safety compliance. You will provide electrical design and coordination for various projects, with a focus on medium and low voltage power distribution, motor controls, lighting, and grounding systems, particularly for water and wastewater projects. The ideal candidate demonstrates the ability to manage multiple assignments simultaneously while meeting project deadlines and completing task-driven objectives. They bring experience in applying instrumentation and controls to process and electromechanical equipment, along with a basic understanding of industrial network design and implementation. Basic knowledge of AutoCAD and Revit, as well as proficiency in Microsoft Office applications—including Word, Excel, MS Project, and Outlook—is important. Travel is required to support project needs, primarily in the Columbus area, and may constitute approximately 5 to 10% of your time. A valid driver's license, a clean driving record, and a willingness to travel for site-specific services are essential for success in this role.Qualifications & Experience:Required QualificationsActively pursuing bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or closely related engineering field.Preferred QualificationsLocal candidates preferredWhy Arcadis?We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It's why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.You'll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you'll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.Together, we can create a lasting legacy.Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & BelongingWe want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.Arcadis offers benefits for part-time, as-needed positions. jobs.title: Building Project Engineer Intern - Summer 2027 at Journey Group
jobs.description: Employer: Journey Group - Journey Construction, A Division of Journey Group Expires: 10/03/2026 OUR OPENINGAre you looking to gain hands-on experience in the construction industry? Join Journey Construction, a division of Journey Group in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, as a Seasonal Project Engineer Intern for Summer 2027. Working onsite, you'll have the opportunity to immerse yourself in various construction projects, learning from seasoned professionals while contributing to real-world endeavors. Grow your skills, build your network, and make an impact in a dynamic work environment. JOURNEY GROUP: OUR STORYJourney Group is a full-service construction group with headquarters in Sioux Falls, S.D., and four divisions offering commercial, manufacturing, industrial, civil, residential and asphalt construction services in the upper Midwest and nationwide. Our company has a long-standing reputation of building lasting relationships with contractors throughout the region. Our experience in past projects working in and around the local construction market coupled with our solid reputation of being a fair, honest, and team-oriented company will bring a strong contractor interest to any project. With Journey Group, you're getting engineers and construction professionals with a wealth of education and experience-but you're also getting allies on your project site. Our team is trustworthy, communicative, fiscally responsible and never lacking in follow-through.WHAT WOULD YOU DO AS A PROJECT ENGINEER INTERN?As a Project Engineer Intern at Journey Construction, you will have the invaluable opportunity to delve into various facets of construction, from mastering scheduling and cost management to enhancing your skills in plan reading, safety protocols, and customer relations. Your responsibilities will entail both administrative tasks and hands-on fieldwork under the guidance of experienced professionals, providing you with a well-rounded experience in the construction industry. This internship is designed to offer you a comprehensive overview of project execution and equip you with the knowledge and skills needed to succeed in a fast-paced construction environment.EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION REQUIREDTo excel in the Project Engineer Intern role at Journey Construction, candidates should be currently pursuing a degree in a construction-related field, ideally at a Junior or Senior standing. Prior experience in the construction industry is advantageous, while familiarity with Microsoft Office is essential for handling project-related tasks efficiently. Candidates must be adept at multitasking, problem-solving, and strong communication skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.Additionally, having the ability to adapt quickly to changing project requirements and a keen eye for detail will contribute to your success in this dynamic internship opportunity. Don't miss this chance to gain hands-on experience and grow your construction career with us!WORK ENVIRONMENT / PHYSICAL DEMANDSThe work environment is representative of what an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made.Mix of Office / Field:Work performed either in the field on job sites 75% with some office time 25%.Some work takes place in an indoor office setting equipped with a computer, desk, phone, and other typical office equipment. Must be able to inspect details at close range, interact, communicate, and exchange accurate information consistently.Must be able to consistently move about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly on job sites with unfinished and uneven surfaces.Some work takes place in outdoor weather conditions.Must be able to retain a stationary position for extended periods of time occasionally depending on the task.Must be able to transfer materials ranging from the ground to overhead occasionally.Must be able to move material up to 50 lbs. occasionally.Must be able to safely use hand and power tools or other safety equipment on occasion. OUR TEAM NEEDS YOU!If you are ready to join our mission of positively impacting lives by building community, please submit a resume online or stop in and fill out an application at 4500 W 58th Street Sioux Falls, SD 57108.Journey Group is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE) and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding hiring and employment. Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law.

jobs.description: Employer: Greenheck Group Expires: 10/03/2026 We are looking for a highly motivated Engineering student to join our team as an Engineering Co-op in Central Wisconsin from January to August OR May to December. Greenheck Group is a dynamic, multi-branded international commercial HVAC manufacturer. Our equipment is used worldwide in commercial, institutional, and industrial facilities, ranging from comfort ventilation to manufacturing processes. Our efficient products improve comfort, safety, and health of lives across the planet. Since 1947, we are deeply committed to helping you “Build Your Future,” through professional growth, challenging projects, and exciting opportunities to explore your career path. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOINGAs an Engineering Co-op you'll be working in one of the following functional areas based on your skills, interests, major, and business need. Test Engineering - You will be responsible for building prototypes, conducting tests, and documenting results. You will play a key role in developing new products, redesigns, and customer-driven requests, with most of your time spent in our testing lab for a truly hands-on experience. Manufacturing Engineering - You will support daily production by creating and updating Standard Operating Procedures, troubleshooting machines, and driving continuous improvement initiatives. You’ll also contribute to layout design and process development to enhance efficiency, quality, and safety across our operations. Product Engineering - You will guide our products from initial concept to market launch. This involves designing, testing, and overseeing the production of new and existing products, ensuring they meet market needs and company goals. Working across research, design, and manufacturing, you’ll ensure products deliver real value to customers and align with company goals. Application Engineering - You will support product development by conducting market research, analyzing customer needs, and assisting with product selection software design and testing. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams - including engineering, product management, marketing, manufacturing, sales, and operations - to improve products, develop training and marketing materials, and contribute to product strategy, customer value, and continuous improvement. WHAT YOU SHOULD HAVEEnrollment in a related bachelor’s degree program (Mechanical, Industrial, Technology, Manufacturing or Applied Engineering etc.) On track to graduate in the next 3 semesters or less Interest in hands-on learning Curiosity and willingness to learn in a fast-paced, innovative environment Experience working with basic hand tools Experience with 3D modeling software (a plus) to expand your technical toolkit and design capabilities Strong problem-solving and analytical skills to support customer-focused solutions THE EARLY TALENT EXPERIENCEAs part of our Early Talent Program, you'll have opportunities to:Develop Your Career: Gain meaningful, real-world experience while working full-time (40 hours a week) throughout your 8-month co-op term.Explore Our Business: Participate in Fundamental Fridays to learn about different areas of the business and hear directly from leaders across the company.Collaborate Across the Company: Be an important part of your team while building relationships and collaborating with others across the organization.Build Your Network: Connect with interns and co-ops across the U.S. and build relationships with approximately 90 fellow college students.Grow Through Feedback: Receive meaningful feedback and coaching throughout your experience, including mid-term and final performance reviews.Connect with Leaders: Share your projects and experiences with company leaders and executives at the end of your term.Make a Difference: Give back through company-sponsored volunteer opportunities and make an impact in our communities. COMPENSATION & BENEFITSGreenheck Group takes pride in providing competitive pay. The pay range for this position is $22.00/hour - $28.00/hour, based on position and academic year.In addition to competitive pay, co-ops and interns receive paid time off for company-observed holidays and are eligible for additional financial support, which may include company-provided housing, a housing allowance, or a sign-on bonus, depending on location, assignment, and length of term. jobs.title: Cybersecurity and Privacy Intern - Summer 2027 - Los Angeles at Grant Thornton
jobs.description: Employer: Grant Thornton Expires: 10/03/2026 Please apply to the one position/location you are most interested in. In order to be considered for this position, you must apply through the Grant Thornton Job portal at www.grantthornton.com/careers(including resume and transcript). Who is Grant Thornton? At Grant Thornton, we believe in making business more personal and building trust into every result – for our clients and you. Here, we go beyond your expectations of a career in professional services by offering a career path with more: more opportunity, more flexibility, and more support. It’s what makes us different, and we think being different makes us better. In the U.S., Grant Thornton delivers professional services through two specialized entities: Grant Thornton LLP, a licensed, certified public accounting (CPA) firm that provides audit and assurance services ― and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (not a licensed CPA firm), which exclusively provides non-attest offerings, including tax and advisory services. In 2025, Grant Thornton formed a multinational, multidisciplinary platform with Grant Thornton Ireland. The platform offers a premier Trans-Atlantic advisory and tax practice, as well as independent American and Irish audit practices. With $2.7 billion in revenues and more than 50 offices spanning the U.S., Ireland and other territories, the platform delivers a singular client experience that includes enhanced solutions and capabilities, backed by powerful technologies and a roster of 12,000 quality-driven professionals enjoying exceptional career-growth opportunities and a distinctive cross-border culture. Grant Thornton is part of the Grant Thornton International Limited network, which provides access to its member firms in more than 150 global markets. Why become a Cybersecurity and Privacy Intern at Grant Thornton? With the rise in Cyber breaches across industries, companies are aggressively looking for consultants to help them protect their critical assets and proactively prepare and respond to these events. The threat actors have shifted from simple, nuisance based Cyber hacks to criminals, activists, ransom hacks and nation states. Additionally, as data privacy regulations tighten and personal data becomes an increasingly valuable target, the need to safeguard sensitive information from unauthorized access and ensure compliance with privacy laws has never been more critical. Our Cybersecurity & Privacy practice provides a unique opportunity to leverage your technology background while expanding your business and project management skills in a dynamic and challenging environment. As part of our team, you’ll work on diverse projects across our Cybersecurity & Privacy services portfolio. These projects include Cyber program strategies, identity and access management, ethical hacking, Cyber incident management, detection, and response, cloud security, privacy regulatory compliance, cookie and consent management, data protection, and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in Cybersecurity & Privacy solutions. Interested candidates should have analytical skills, be strong “thinkers”, with an affinity for learning and innovation. Interested candidates should be self-starters and should demonstrate strength in or a desire to build skills related to Grant Thornton’s core values of: Collaboration, Leadership, Excellence, Agility, Respect, and Responsibility. Your day-to-day may include: Interns can expect to work closely with the Cybersecurity & Privacy team on all phases of the engagement lifecycle including planning, engagement management, and project wrap-up. Some of the typical projects are: Cyber Strategy and Program Design. Business Strategy and Cyber Strategy Alignment. Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Cybersecurity & Privacy. Privacy Compliance Program. Cookie and Consent Management. Data Protection. Cloud Security. Identity and Access Management. Cyber Threat Monitoring. Cyber Incident Management. Cyber War Gaming. Ethical Hacking. In addition, interns are expected to actively contribute to business growth by identifying business development opportunities, participating in marketing and brand initiatives, and assisting with the development of Grant Thornton thought leadership. You have the following technical skills or qualifications: Pursuing a degree in one of the following: B.S. in Engineering within Computer, Computer Science, Information Systems. B.S. in Computer Science. B.S. program in Data analytics, Informatics, Management with Cybersecurity (minor). B.S. program with a specialization in Technology – “Hands on technology experience”. B.S. in Cybersecurity or Information Security. Optional – Juris Doctorate (J.D.) degree with interest in Cybersecurity and Data Privacy. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0/4.0. Demonstrated digital fluency through the effective use of technology, data, and basic AI technologies to enhance productivity and decision-making Ability to travel as required. Strong business and technical aptitude and problem-solving skills. Likes to learn the business of our clients to help them solve problems. Ability to bridge the gap between business strategy, technology, and Cybersecurity & Privacy compliance requirements to help deliver sustainable solutions to our clients. Excellent thinking, analytical, communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills. Effective time management skills for handling multiple priorities and simultaneous projects. Enthusiasm to learn through a combination of structured, on-the-job, and self-directed training. Ability to work efficiently and effectively in a team environment. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. No visa sponsorship is available for this position. The team you’re about to join is ready to help you thrive. Here’s how: Whether it’s your work location, weekly schedule or flex time off, we empower you with the options to work in the way that best serves your clients and your life. Consistent with the firm’s hybrid work model, this position will require in-person attendance at least three days per week, either at a GT office or client site. Here, you are supported to prioritize your overall well-being through work-life integration options that work best for you and those in your household. We understand that your needs, responsibilities and experiences are different — and we think that’s a good thing. That’s why we support you with personalized and comprehensive benefits that recognize and empower all the identities, roles and aspirations that make you, well, you. See how at www.gt.com/careers. When it comes to inclusion, we are committed to doing more than checking boxes. Explore all the ways we’re taking action for diversity, equity & inclusion at www.gt.com/careers. Here’s what you can expect next: If you apply and are selected to interview, a Grant Thornton team member will reach out to you to schedule a time to connect. We encourage you to also check out other roles that may be a good fit for you or get to know us a little bit better at www.gt.com/careers. Benefits: We understand that your needs, responsibilities and experiences are different, and we think that’s a good thing. That’s why we support you with personalized and comprehensive benefits that recognize and empower all the identities, roles and aspirations that make you, well, you. For an overview of our benefit offerings, please visit: https://www.grantthornton.com/careers/rewards-and-benefits. Benefits for internship positions: Grant Thornton interns are eligible to participate in the firm’s medical, dental and vision insurance programs and the firm’s employee assistance program. Interns also receive a minimum of 72 hours of paid sick leave, and are paid for firm holidays that fall within their internship period. Benefits for seasonal employee positions: Grant Thornton seasonal employees are eligible to participate in the firm’s medical, dental and vision insurance programs and the firm’s employee assistance program. Seasonal employees may also be eligible to participate in the firm’s 401(k) savings plan and employee retirement plan in accordance with applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements. Seasonal employees receive a minimum of 72 hours of paid sick leave. Grant Thornton employees may be eligible for a discretionary, annual bonus based on individual and firm performance, subject to the terms, conditions and eligibility criteria of the applicable bonus plan or program. Interns and seasonal employees are not eligible for bonus compensation. Additional Details: It is the policy of Grant Thornton to promote equal employment opportunities. All personnel decisions (including, but not limited to, recruiting, hiring, training, working conditions, promotion, transfer, compensation, benefits, evaluations, and termination) are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital or civil union status, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship status, veteran status, disability, handicap, genetic predisposition or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state and local laws, it is the policy of Grant Thornton to provide reasonable accommodation when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with a disability, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship. The policy regarding requests for reasonable accommodation applies to all aspects of employment, including the application process. To make an accommodation request, please contact HR@us.gt.com. For Los Angeles Applicants only: We will consider for employment all qualified Applicants, including those with Criminal Histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance. The pay rate for this position in the firm’s Los Angeles, California office is $40 per hour.

jobs.description: Employer: Ameriprise Financial Expires: 10/03/2026 Job DescriptionPlease note that applications will be assessed on a rolling basis. Due to anticipated interest, the role may close earlier than the stated deadline. We recommend submitting your application promptly. The advertised closing date is October 3, 2026. At Ameriprise Financial, Columbia Threadneedle Investments, and RiverSource, we're committed to helping early-career talent grow through meaningful work and practical learning. Whether you're joining us as an Intern or Leadership Development Program participant, you'll work alongside experienced colleagues, contribute fresh perspectives, and gain exposure to the people, projects, and experiences that drive our business forward. Guided by our core values of putting clients first, acting with integrity, striving for excellence, and respecting individuals and our communities, you'll develop both professionally and personally. Through mentoring, networking, senior leader engagement, and community initiatives, you'll build valuable skills, expand your network, and discover what's possible across a global financial organization. About the Role:Ameriprise Financial has a global Technology team delivering technology solutions to support the evolving needs of our clients, advisors and employees. As a Technology Intern, you are assigned to a specific Technology team for the 10-week summer internship. Technology internship teams and responsibilities vary each year. For the 2027 summer internship program, we are seeking one intern for each of the following Technology teams:Analytics & AutomationEnd User ComputingCloud EngineeringSoftware Engineering (DevSecOps)Data Warehouse & AnalyticsInformation Security Tools How you’ll spend your time…As a Technology intern, you will gain hands-on experience with Ameriprise tools, applications, and technologies while contributing to solutions that support the team’s goals and priorities. During the summer, you’ll connect with other Technology interns and LDPs on a regular basis to foster community and build your professional network. At the end of your internship, you will present an overview of your internship and accomplishments to our Technology leadership team. As an intern, responsibilities vary depending on assigned team and may include:Define business requirementsDevelop, document, test, and modify new or existing codeDevelop working knowledge of Ameriprise systems, processes, data, and vendor toolsLearn and apply standard techniques, procedures, and criteria to the software development life cycleLearn new programming languagesIdentify opportunities for process improvement or automationParticipate in Agile team ceremonies Examples of past intern work includes:Automated cloud activity monitoringAutomated test frameworkCustomer analytics analysisCloud storage relationship model proof of conceptInactive account auditing and decommissionAutomation of server start-up/shutdown and testingCreate dashboard reporting using PowerBICreate new intake and tracking systemSharePoint development Required Qualifications:Current Junior at a 4-year university pursing a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer/Software Engineering, Computer Information Science, Information Technology Infrastructure, or related technical field.Graduation date of December 2027 or May/June 2028Interested in gaining broad experience in TechnologyProven organization skills and ability to manage time effectivelyAbility to work and communicate collaboratively and constructively with othersProficient with Microsoft Office Suite If you also had this, it would be great:High degree of self-motivation with strong integrity and ethicsExcellent communication, interpersonal, and presentation skillsDisplays a positive attitude, professionalism, and a willingness to learn in a corporate environmentPrior classroom, project, or work experience with software development/programming/coding Visa SponsorshipApplicants must have a valid work authorization that does not now, or in the future, require visa sponsorship for employment in the United States (e.g., H-1B, F-1 CPT, F-1 OPT, TN). In-Office Collaboration We are a client-centric, relationship-based business. Working together, in-person, is foundational to how we achieve results. By fostering a culture of face-to-face collaboration, idea sharing, productivity and personal connection, we deliver for our stakeholders — clients, advisors, employees and shareholders. Our employees work in the office at least four (4) days per week, with flexibility to work from home one (1) day per week. Some roles may require additional in-office time or different in-office expectations, and specific requirements will be discussed during the hiring process. Base Pay Salary The estimated hourly rate for this role is $35.00 per hour. We have a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy. Your initial total compensation may vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and geographical work location. In addition, most of our roles are eligible for variable pay in the form of bonus, commissions, and/or long-term incentives depending on the role. We also have a competitive and comprehensive benefits program that supports all aspects of your health and well-being, including but not limited to vacation time, sick time, 401(k), and health, dental and life insurance. jobs.title: Civil Engineering Scholar - Culpeper, VA at Virginia Department of Transportation
jobs.description: Employer: Virginia Department of Transportation Expires: 10/04/2026 Kick-start your career with VDOT! VDOT’s Civil Engineering Scholarship Program offers civil engineering students the opportunity to gain valuable, real-world work experience, earn money over the summer, and receive fall and spring semester stipends of $3,500 to assist with educational expenses. Scholar Program participants spend summers working in a challenging and interesting VDOT position, receiving hands-on work experience within a variety of disciplines and geographic areas, under the direction of a professional engineer. Upon graduation, scholars transition into the Employee Development and Growth Experience (EDGE) Program, a full-time, one or two-year position with varied work assignments. Stipends are issued based on continued program eligibility. VDOT will disperse the funds prior to the start of each semester. jobs.description: Employer: City of Urbandale, IA Expires: 10/04/2026 The Urbandale Fire Department (UFD) is now accepting applications for the 2026-2027 Firefighter/EMS Pathway Internship Program.The Pathway Program is designed for individuals who are beginning their careers in the fire and emergency medical services and have not yet obtained all the certifications required to become a Firefighter/EMT or Firefighter/Paramedic. The program provides participants with an opportunity to gain valuable knowledge, skills, and practical experience while working toward completion of their required fire and EMS certifications. This temporary part-time program has two levels: Intern Level – Non-CertifiedFor candidates who do not currently hold an EMS or Firefighter certification but are enrolled in an accredited fire or EMS training program.Cert 1 Level – Certified For candidates who currently hold an EMS or Firefighter certification.Current Starting Pay:Intern – Non-Certified: $18.17/hourCert 1 – Firefighter only: $18.17/hourCert 1 – EMT only: $18.99/hourCert 1 – Paramedic only: $21.77/hourCandidates who are accepted into the program will be required to work shifts while simultaneously working towards obtaining their fire and EMS certifications. Pathway Program participants will be expected to demonstrate continued progress in both on-the-job performance and the completion of required certifications within designated timeframes. Successful completion of the Pathway Program may provide an opportunity to advance into a regular part-time position with the Urbandale Fire Department.The mission of the Urbandale Fire Department is to preserve life, protect property, and promote safety. With three fire stations strategically located across the city, we respond to more than 6,400 calls per year. Through our automatic aid agreements with six neighboring metro departments, participants have the opportunity to train alongside highly experienced professionals in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. The UFD is proud to be internationally accredited by the Commission on Fire Accreditation International (CFAI) - a distinction that recognizes our commitment to excellence in fire and emergency services. We are also deeply committed to community engagement and public education, helping to reduce risk and increase safety awareness throughout Urbandale. This recruitment is for the Pathway Internship Program only. Fully certified candidates are ineligible for the Pathway Program. Certified candidates seeking part-time or full-time employment are encouraged to submit an Interest Card. Familiarity with department policies and procedures.Performs vehicle/squad checks and completes vehicle and station routine maintenance and inventory.Performs annual equipment testing.Performs annual or semi-annual cleaning and maintenance on apparatus, equipment, and facilities.Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned. Provides accurate medical documentation of all emergency medical treatment provided, including the use of table-based patient care reporting systems. Completes patient care reporting requirements, including patient medical history, incident history, and billing information.Ensures fire code enforcement by participating in fire/life safety facility inspections, including the field use of tablet-based safety inspection documentation.Under direct supervision, performs routine truck and equipment maintenance, station maintenance and routine facility duties, including the use of tablet-based inventory and vehicle maintenance program.As part of a crew, performs various community education or community risk reduction activities to improve safety for the community and enhance the reputation of the department. Provided the opportunity to participate in physical fitness activities. To their level of certification, participates in fire/EMS training. Cert 1 Level – CertifiedEMS or Firefighter Certification: Must possess one of the following:A valid Iowa EMT or Paramedic certification;A valid National Registry EMT or Paramedic certification;A valid Iowa Firefighter I certification through FSTB; orA valid out-of-state Firefighter I certification through IFSAC or Pro Board.Must possess a valid driver's license.Must provide documentation demonstrating a passing score (70% or higher) on the IO Solutions National Firefighter Selection Inventory (NSFI) exam received on or after September 4, 2025.Must be able to meet all physical standards for the job as specified by the Fire Retirement System.Must be able to perform physical functions of the job while wearing personal protective equipment.Ability to work a minimum of 24 hours per week.Must be able to pass post-offer/pre-employment: professional reference checks, drug screening, physical, motor vehicle report check, and background check.For a complete list of desired knowledge, skills, and abilities, please refer to the job description.Supplemental InformationCandidates will receive notifications via email from www.governmentjobs.com (NEOGOV). jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 10/04/2026 Records Management Fellow - State, Tribal, and Local Plans & Grants DivisionSummary American Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with the National Park Service is seeking one Records Management Fellow to assist STLPG (State, Tribal, and Local Plans & Grants) division staff with cultural resource programs through grants to states, tribes, territories, and other eligible recipients that support the preservation of America's historic places and history. Start Date: 11/30/2026End Date: 7/6/2027* a 32-week commitment is required for this positionLocation Details/Description: Remote or onsite in Washington, D.C.The State, Tribal, and Local Plans & Grants Division (STLPG), located in Washington D.C., provides preservation assistance through a number of Historic Preservation Fund grant programs that support the preservation of America's historic places and diverse history. This position is onsite based out of D.C. with some opportunities for telework. The position will allow for up to 60% telework but the fellow must be available to be onsite for the necessary projects.For more information about the State, Tribal, Local Plans & Grants Division, please visit the NPS website.Position Overview: State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (STLPG) is a national program at National Park Service (NPS) headquarters office that supports cultural resource programs through grants to states, tribes, territories, and other eligible recipients. The source of funding for the grants is Congressional appropriations from the Historic Preservation Fund. The fellow will work directly with NPS staff in parks and/or programs around Washington, DC to assist in the management of grant projects, primarily of archival or museum collections.The ACE Fellow:Reviews applications for grant programs, primarily of the collections or history project types and makes recommendations for funding for awarding officerDrafts the award certificate package for applications recommended for funding by grant programsMake recommendations on scope and budget review of selected applications and drafts grant agreements for awarding officerReviews grant deliverables, primarily of the collections or history project types, and makes recommendations on approval to awarding officerCorresponds with grantees as directed by the awarding officer to connect grantees with answers to queries or published guidanceAppraises and arranges Federal records, assists with transferring records to Federal Records Centers and/or the National ArchivesCoordinates and carries out recommendations for digitization of recordsPlans, organizes, and promotes records maintenance and disposition within the divisionThe Fellow will have the opportunity to:Learn grants management practices and processes for managing federal cultural resource grantsAcquire skills in reviewing applications and grant deliverablesDevelop communication skills with grant professionals, internal and externalParticipate in grant manager meetingsLearn records management and archival best practices for managing cultural resource collections and Federal records Acquire skills in appraising, arranging, and inventorying collections of Federal records Apply knowledge of records management disposition schedules and procedures when transferring records to Federal Records Centers and/or the National ArchivesTraining Provided: In addition to the operational responsibilities, there will also be an important educational component. Training opportunities may include:Grants management and financial assistance statutes, regulations, policies, and practices of the federal government and the National Park Service.Archival and collections management specific practices for the National Park Service program operations of the Cultural Resources Directorate, STLPG division.Site tours of grant projects within the Washington, DC area, within travel budget allowance, or where other opportunities allow.Leadership and project management skill developmentThis individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promotes exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. This could include gaining experience in different conservation fields and shadowing different work groups.This individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promotes exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets.WHO WE AREFor nearly 70 years, Cupertino Electric, Inc. (CEI) has been powered by people who’ve built a reputation for delivering high-profile, complex projects. Real, tangible things that alter the landscape and improve lives. But even more than that, we’ve built a reputation for integrity. We’re problem solvers and innovation seekers. We’re team players and safety fanatics. And we always—always—do the right thing. Even when no one is looking. Because what we do here is important, but how we do it is everything. JOB SUMMARYThis paragraph summarizes the general nature, level, and purpose of the job. The Internship Program at Cupertino Electric, Inc. is a 10-to-12-week program designed to expose undergraduate and post-graduate students to various aspects of CEI’s core markets: Commercial, Data Center, and Energy & Renewables. The program offers students unique opportunities to contribute to real-world projects and make meaningful industry connections. Although we are headquartered in California, we have major projects and offices in many other states including Ohio, Iowa, Wisconsin, New Mexico, and Utah. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONSThe essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned. Employees must abide by all requirements including but not limited to sensitivity to cultural diversity, safety and security of physical environments, emergency management, teamwork, respect for others, participation in ongoing education and training, communication and adherence to safety programs, and licensure and health screenings. Must perform all duties and responsibilities in accordance with the standards of Cupertino Electric, Inc. jobs.description: Employer: Centrus Energy Expires: 10/05/2026 Job Summary:Ready to experience how large-scale engineering and manufacturing projects come to life? As a Recycle and Assembly Intern at Centrus Energy, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to the planning and execution of complex infrastructure and plant projects that support advanced uranium enrichment and facility operations. Working alongside experienced managers, supervisors and technicians you’ll see how engineering design, procurement coordination, and manufacturing come together to deliver mission-critical projects. This internship provides a unique opportunity to understand the manufacture, assembly and delivery of centrifuges for uranium enrichment while building administrative, technical and professional skills that will accelerate your career. What You Will Do:Step into the world of manufacturing, assembly and construction efforts related to the enrichment of uranium. As a Recycle and Assembly Intern you will assist managers, supervisors and technicians in reviewing design documents, design documents, tracking project schedules, supporting technical documentation, coordinating with quality control, engineering and assembly teams. jobs.title: Analytical Technology Intern at Johns Manville
jobs.description: Employer: Johns Manville Expires: 10/05/2026 The Analytical Technologies team at Johns Manville tackles whatever problem arises across all three of JM’s businesses (Engineered Products, Roofing Systems and Insulation Systems) as well as supporting R&D efforts and product development through measurement science ranging from physicochemical properties analysis of raw materials to product testing and characterization. The team is looking for a Materials Science focused Analytical Chemistry or Engineering student with an interest in materials characterization. This intern will be expected to employ fundamental concepts of chemistry and physics in a wholistic, hands-on approach to support product development and operational excellence in line with JM’s sustainability goals of increasing recycled waste streams as raw materials. This work will include pre-planned laboratory-scale measurements using analytical instrumentation. The internship is designed to provide flexibility for the intern to help progress the project by following what they’ve learned and to guide the scientific experimentation based on their initial results with the ultimate project goal in mind. Upon completion of the summer internship, this JM intern is expected to present their work within the context of their scientific study, business relevance and sustainability to senior management. The leadership team then provides valuable feedback and insight for interns as they continue their careers. What You Bring to the Team:Enrolled in a B.S. program in Materials Science, Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Physics or related field, and have completed analytical and/or instrumental chemistry.Experience with analytical data analysis, statistics analysis software and data interpretation.Ability to work within a team, communicate effectively and clearly provide honest constructive feedback.Have a creative mindset for exploring problems beyond the immediate task at hand, intrinsic drive to push beyond road-blocks that hinder progress in a project, and ability to pivot from initial experimental trajectories when unexpected results are encountered. Your Day to Day:Perform relevant analytical measurements using scientific instrumentation and interpret the results.Consider how laboratory scale results from scientific instrumentation can be extrapolated to industrial scale production in relation to a specified product.Take an active part in weekly meetings to discuss involvement in support of plant operations, R&D efforts, product development projects, raw materials characterization, and associated experimental planning.Provide services or recommendations for the use of appropriate scientific instrumentation to measure the properties of materials required by a project lead. Preferred Qualifications:Experience with laboratory scale scientific analytical instrumentation to characterize materials. May include differential scanning calorimetry, dynamic mechanical analysis, oscillatory shear and/or capillary rheology, thermogravimetric analysis, gas chromatography, pyrolysis-mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography, gel permeation chromatography, Fourier transform infrared or Raman spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, Instron mechanical properties testing, cone calorimetry, UV-Vis spectrophotometry, or other instrumentation.

jobs.description: Employer: Evergy Expires: 10/05/2026 SUMMARY OF JOB RESPONSIBILITIES AND REQUIREMENTS JOB TITLE: Intern – Transmission Line Engineering REQUISITION: TRA0106DEPARTMENT: Transmission Engineering – Topeka General OfficeLOCATION: Topeka, KSPAY RANGE: $23.00 - $28.00 / Hour Full-Time Internship Position for Summer 2027 Scheduled Work Hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. (Other hours as required) It's never too early to start exploring your future career. If you're ready to apply the principles you've been learning in the classroom to real-world projects, Evergy is for you. Hands-on experience is what our internship programs are all about. Our programs provide students with meaningful experience while helping Evergy identify talented future full-time employees. Many of our interns transition to successful careers at Evergy.Evergy interns are trusted contributors on active design projects. In addition to project work, Evergy interns participate in many social and extra-curricular activities, including volunteer events, power plant tours, Lunch-and-Learns, and more. Intern Description:This position joins a skilled, energetic, and engaging team of engineers who perform all aspects of high-voltage (69kV-345kV) transmission line design; a fast-paced, dynamic, and highly specialized engineering discipline. Each “T-line” project is unique. The long, linear nature of these facilities requires engineers to solve a variety of challenges, making thoughtful engineering judgment as valuable as technical analysis. Interns are trusted contributors on active engineering projects. They gain exposure to coordinating and collaborating with professionals in other departments and work locations. Interns participate in technical conversations and meetings with project managers and other professionals on the project team. They visit Evergy transmission line projects in the field before, during, and after construction. Construction site visits provide the opportunity to see transmission linemen, some of the most highly skilled and valued workers in the construction industry, at their craft. Typical intern responsibilities include:Perform detailed line design and analysis using PLS-CADD and PLS-POLE, highly sophisticated finite element software packages used exclusively for transmission line engineering.Create structure loading drawings and review vendor-produced calculations and structure drawings.Design and analyze transmission line foundation systems, including deep drilled piers and embedded structures.Conduct construction site visits to perform safety observations and gain familiarity with the practical application of engineering deliverables.Incorporate and interpret transmission line survey data, including aerial LiDAR, ground survey information, and easement exhibits.Collaborate with the transmission line engineering team and other Evergy teams, including Permitting & Environmental, Substation Engineering, Real Estate, Project Management, and Construction & Maintenance.Prepare construction drawings, bill of material packages, and supporting construction documents.Analyze existing facility structural capacity and electrical clearance margins in accordance with code and company standards. Education and Experience Requirements:Candidates must be currently enrolled in a university with an ABET-accredited engineering program in one of the following or a related technical field: Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Electrical Engineering. Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities Required:A demonstrated ability to overcome challenges and contribute effectively as part of a collaborative project team.An inquisitive, analytical mindset, with a desire to understand the reasoning behind design standards and the perspectives of diverse stakeholders.Strong organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.Understanding of fundamental engineering principles and advanced mathematics.Proficiency with spreadsheets, word processing, and database software.Ability to evaluate, select, and apply standard engineering techniques, procedures, and criteria while exercising sound engineering judgment. Working Conditions:Primarily an office setting with standard business hours (Monday-Friday). Periodic visits to transmission line and substation field environments are also expected. jobs.title: Summer Safety Associate (Summer 2027) at Clark Construction Group
jobs.description: Employer: Clark Construction Group Expires: 10/05/2026 The Summer Associate – Safety role provides you with the unique opportunity to safeguard the health and well-being of thousands of craft workers and team members across our jobsites. Working directly alongside Clark’s safety and operational leaders, you will gain hands-on field experience advancing company safety policies, programs, and procedures while actively driving our 24/7 "Culture of Care.” We empower you to take on significant responsibility early, backing your growth with extensive resources, mentorship, formal training, and a culture that challenges you to advance your career further. Here, the standard is higher. Our team doesn't just build landmark projects—we build the leaders who make them possible. The Role The Summer Associate Program is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of the construction industry and our business. As a summer associate, you will be fully embedded with a team on a jobsite or in a department, gaining hands-on experience. Beyond your project work, you will become an integrated member of the Clark community through training and development opportunities. Build your network through social events and jobsite tours, and sharpen your skills with formal training sessions led by Clark experts. Other cornerstones of the Summer Associate Program include: The Capstone Project: A team-based project that challenges you to develop innovative solutions for real-time business opportunities. You will present your findings directly to company leadership, gaining visibility and the chance to make a tangible impact. The Passport Experience: A curated series of experiences designed to guide your summer journey. The Passport showcases the full breadth of Clark’s business, helps you establish meaningful connections across the company, and ensures you gain essential industry knowledge. This immersive, full-time program runs for 8 -10 weeks and begins in late May or early June. Responsibilities Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to: Program Implementation: Assisting in executing corporate and project-specific safety and health programs in alignment with federal, state, and local safety standards.Culture & Education: Helping promote a proactive safety culture by coaching, mentoring, and educating trade partners and internal team members on occupational health and safety requirements.Field Inspections & Analytics: Conducting daily jobsite walks to monitor safety compliance, track metrics, and assist in reporting project safety performance and forward-looking plans.Safety Planning: Partnering closely with field superintendents and project leadership to plan for high-risk operations, including critical crane lifts, hazardous material handling, fire prevention, and site evacuation strategies. Basic QualificationsCurrently attending university and working to complete a bachelor's degree in Occupational Health and SafetyInterest and passion for the construction industry The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings. Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations. Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines. A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly. Clark offers a total compensation package. Benefits could include commuter benefits or fitness reimbursement. Hourly rates will be determined by factors such as geographic location, education, experience, and market considerations. For this role the hourly rate is $23 - $29/ hr.

jobs.description: Employer: Wellington Management Company LLP Expires: 10/06/2026 WELLINGTON MANAGEMENTWellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Designed for students from a variety of academic backgrounds, this program is intended for candidates with prior experience in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related technical field who want to apply those skills to building practical technology solutions. Interns will have the opportunity to explore career paths in Wellington’s technology organization and do meaningful work alongside experienced professionals. What You'll DoAs a summer intern, you will work alongside a cohort of fellow interns on a summer-long project focused on building a software solution that addresses a real business challenge at Wellington. Working as part of a project team, you'll gain hands-on experience in software engineering, data analysis, and product-oriented problem solving while developing technical, professional, and leadership skills. If you are a candidate with a disability, or are assisting a candidate with a disability, and require an accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, please email us at GMWTalentOperations@wellington.com At Wellington Management, our approach to compensation is designed to help us attract, inspire and retain the best talent in our industry. The base salary range for this position is: $19-$35 per hourThis range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered when making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets; role; skills and experience; certifications; and education.
